old: हे अध्वर्युओ, जिसने जलों को घेरने वाले वृत्र को मारा, जैसे वज्र वृक्ष को; उसके लिए इसे लाओ, जो उसे चाहता है; यह इन्द्र इसके पान के योग्य है।
new: हे अध्वर्युओ, जिसने जलों को घेरने वाले वृत्र को मारा, जैसे अशनि वृक्ष को; उसके लिए इसे लाओ, जो उसे चाहता है; यह इन्द्र इसके पान के योग्य है।
why: reviewer (minor): aśanī is 'thunderbolt' (English); vajra is a fixed separate rendering, so Hindi 'वज्र' for aśani blurs the two words.
reviewer (minor): w must be the dictionary-style form: ya is yaḥ before u- (as in every other unit of this hymn).

reviewer (minor): A masculine a-stem accusative would end in -am; rudhikrām is the accusative of the feminine name Rudhikrā, so 'm.' is wrong (the Hindi/English only give the name, so no change there).

old: O Adhvaryu priests, make ready service for him; lift up the purified Soma in the wood. Enjoying, he bellows to you toward what is in the hand; offer the intoxicating Soma to Indra.
new: O Adhvaryu priests, make ready service for him; lift up the purified one in the wood. Enjoying, he bellows to you toward what is in the hand; offer the intoxicating Soma to Indra.
why: reviewer (minor): nipūtam stands alone in the line; 'Soma' is supplied. (The Hindi correctly has only 'शुद्ध किए हुए को'.)
reviewer (minor): Gloss 'him' contradicts its gram '(part.)'; it is unrendered in English and Hindi, so treat as a particle.

old: To us, O good one, bring about that bounty for giving; much is your wealth. Indra, that which is wondrous, desiring glory day after day, may we, rich in heroes, speak loudly at the rite.
new: To us, O good one, bring about that bounty for giving; much is your wealth. Indra, that which is wondrous, desiring glory day after day, may we, rich in heroes, speak greatly in the rite.
why: reviewer (minor): The brief's one wording for this refrain is 'may we, rich in heroes, speak greatly in the rite' (bṛhad vadema vidathe suvīrāḥ).
